To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
deacetylated biomass, two-stage pretreatment and a combined yeast inoculum can increase ethanol yield from corn stover and sugar cane bagasse.
Deacetylated cornstover and sugarcance bagasse pretreated with a two stage thermochemical and mechanical process were fermented to ethanol with an optimized yeast blend.
deacetylation of corn stover and blending commercial C5/C6 and non C5/C6 yeasts improved the ethanol yields of both corn stover and bagasse by 6.4% and 7.2% respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the ethanol yield of two of the most abundant and available biomass feedstock in the United States, corn stover and bagasse.
the development of a more efficient process for converting corn stover and bagasse into ethanol.
the improvement of bioethanol production from two of the most promising lignocellulosic feedstocks in the US.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deacetylation pretreatment process and two stage pretreatment process are effective in increasing the fermentable sugars in both corn stover and bagasse.
the deacetylation of corn stover and the combined thermochemical and shear pretreatment of both corn stover and bagasse increased ethanol yield and reduced residual xylose.

the combination of the deacetylation pretreatment and two stage thermochemical and mechanical treatment, followed by fermentation with the optimized inoculation of two commercial yeast strains, resulted in the best performance of all the treatments tested in the current research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

deacetylation and thermochemical pretreatment are two promising pretreatment methods for corn stover and that a combined inoculum containing both a xylose fermenting Saccharomyces and a wild type Saccharomyses is the most efficient inoculation strategy to date for corn stover fermentation.

we have demonstrated that the combination of deacetylation, thermochemical and mechanical pretreatment, and yeast blending can increase the ethanol yield of corn stover by 10% and sugarcane by 6% compared to using the C5 and C6 yeast separately.
the deacetylation and thermochemical and mechanical combined process are the most effective methods to improve the conversion of biomass to ethanol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
blending commercial xylose-fermenting yeast and Saccharomyces cerevisiae wild-type yeast can improve ethanol yield and reduce xylose content in fermentation broths.
the use of a commercial xylose fermentating strain can significantly reduce the residual sugar content in a fermentation broth and improve the ethanol production efficiency.
blending two yeast strains is an effective way to improve the efficiency of biofuel production.
